title: Drive the mute indicator LED from the output volume key
head: d6e303b7fd34
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Localized pactl prints translated yes, so muted LED is cleared on non-English desktops
leads.consequence: PulseAudio pactl v17 get-sink-mute calls pa_yes_no_localised, not a fixed yes/no token. With a French translation, muting via mute-toggle yields Mute: oui; the script's *yes test is false, so the light is driven off while the sink is muted. Unmuting or volume steps also drive it off, correctly for their post-action unmuted state. The existing OSD already mislabels that locale, but this PR newly makes the LED wrong as well. Execute the mute query with LC_ALL=C (or use a stable machine-readable source) and add a locale-aware pactl stub/test; do not merely set the test runner's locale to C and mask the bug.
leads.triage: dropped; Opus ran real pactl under de/fr in private lab: printed 'Mute: yes'; not reproduced; same predicate already drives the pre-existing OSD icon

leads.summary: Writing off to an active audio-mute LED removes its kernel trigger
leads.consequence: On a ThinkPad with [audio-mute] attached (issue #11005 item 4), the first output-unmute or volume step issues brightnessctl set 0. The Linux LED core removes the active trigger, leaving [none]; subsequent ALSA mixer mute changes no longer drive the lamp, even if they previously did. An on write leaves the trigger active and a subsequent ALSA trigger event can overwrite the newly lit state. The targeted author's machine already showed [none], so this does not refute their local result. Discuss taking ownership of the LED intentionally, detect/retain an actually working trigger, or document and test this transition; a success check on a touched brightness fixture cannot detect it.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; coordinator verified led-class.c L75-76 and thinkpad_acpi.c default_trigger

leads.summary: Kernel HDA mute LED devices use hda::mute and are silently excluded
leads.consequence: The kernel's HDA generic LED helper registers hda::mute on supported Realtek/HP codec fixups. On those laptops without platform::mute the guard returns without calling brightnessctl (success status), so this change leaves a real speaker mute indicator unchanged. The optional helper device supports another name, but the output caller never selects it. Choose an actual available supported mute node, preferably with explicit policy for machines exposing both, and add an hda::mute-only fixture.
leads.triage: dropped; guard skips them and their kernel trigger stays attached; Opus confirmed passthrough; scope choice, not a defect

leads.summary: OMARCHY_LEDS_PATH overrides the existence check, not the write target
leads.consequence: With OMARCHY_LEDS_PATH pointing to a fixture and a platform::mute/brightness file present there, brightnessctl still enumerates /sys/class/{backlight,leds}, not that override. If a real platform::mute LED exists, the helper writes the real LED rather than the requested fixture; if no real device exists, it silently does nothing. The test's brightnessctl stub merely logs the command, so it does not catch the split. Either describe the env var as guard-only and never use it as a safe write override, or write to the selected root in the explicitly test-only path.
leads.triage: dropped; matches existing repo sysfs seams (Opus); test stubs brightnessctl

leads.summary: New LED test cannot detect a brightnessctl write failure
leads.consequence: A brightnessctl stub that records the requested command and then exits 1 without changing brightness would satisfy every LED assertion, because the production helper suppresses failure and the test greps only the request log. Users with an existing but unwritable LED still see successful volume/OSD and an unlit LED. Add a test case with a failing brightnessctl and assert the intended failure policy, plus a success-path stub that records the resulting brightness, not only argv. This is a source-level mutant, not an executed reproducer.
leads.triage: dropped; generic test hardening; production uses || true by design; kept in local report

leads.summary: Each volume repeat gains a redundant pactl read and helper launch, including machines without the LED
leads.consequence: The new if volume_muted at line 84 opens a pactl client and launches a helper on every volume step; line 90 opens another pactl client for the same state. The helper launches even without a platform::mute node; when present it additionally launches brightnessctl on every step even if the mute state did not change. Repeating bindings default/hypr/bindings/media.lua:2-3,18-19 amplify it. Cache the mute result for LED and OSD; consider skipping the LED path where no supported device exists or when state is unchanged. This also defeats #6897's explicit write-on-change optimization if both land.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3; published as optional note

leads.summary: Open #6897 installs a second writer for the same LED with a different update policy
leads.consequence: Both heads diverge (compare API), and their changed files do not textually overlap, but the watcher in #6897 follows the same physical sink and writes platform::mute when its state changes while this PR writes after each key event. On a mute key they can each attempt a brightness write; on every volume repeat this PR still writes even when the watcher intentionally suppresses unchanged states. #6897's body explicitly describes its continuous watcher as an alternative to key-only syncing. Decide which owns this LED or coordinate state before merging both; no claim of definite final wrong brightness is made.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus; published as optional note

leads.summary: Open #8096's named non-default sink support would make the default speaker LED follow the wrong sink
leads.consequence: #8096 resolves an explicit second-argument sink name, including the example non-default chat endpoint. Merging its functional change with this unconditional LED tail makes `omarchy-audio-output-volume mute-toggle <non-default-sink>` set the one global platform::mute lamp from the chat sink even if the default music/speaker sink remains audible. The own-base merged copy merges/8096-merged also has a real metadata conflict at lines 3-11: keep both optional sink docs and LED docs when resolving. GitHub's MERGEABLE status is only relative to quattro, not this PR. Gate LED writes on the controlled sink being the effective default, or define explicit multi-sink LED policy.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F4; not published (only if both merge, low)

leads.summary: Open #13494's new mute/unmute metadata directly conflicts with this PR's LED summary
leads.consequence: The diff of #13494 adds menu Mute/Unmute actions, updates the args and examples header, and rewrites the same metadata block this PR rewrites. Applying its own-base merge results in conflict markers at merges/13494-merged:3-11. Resolve headers to include both descriptions/actions, otherwise `omarchy ... --help` can omit the new menu actions or LED claim. The source-level functional changes otherwise coexist and no OSD regression is claimed; #13494's tests need a helper/LED stub when run with this PR on installed hardware.

leads.summary: A failed post-action mute read actively turns the output LED off
leads.consequence: If pactl set-sink-mute succeeds but a following get-sink-mute fails (e.g. audio server disconnect in between), volume_muted returns false and this change calls off, possibly extinguishing the LED while output remains muted. The script then shows its preexisting unmuted OSD, exits according to omarchy-osd, and the LED remains until the next successful key press. This is a conditional failure-path lead; a controlled sink that drops the query would establish frequency and effect. Consider distinguishing an error from a legitimate no before writing off.
leads.triage: dropped; hypothesis, pre-existing OSD behaviour, not reproduced

limits: No PR executable or repository tests were run: this hunt's LED, trigger and merge claims use pinned shell source, fetched upstream kernel v7.2, brightnessctl master source and read-only own-output merged copies. The conditional H8 has not been observed on a running audio server. No source-level success implies a real machine's LED can be written or that an OSD visibly appeared.

flags.claim: which the kernel removes on any write of 0, as every unmute and volume step now does
flags.why: Only unmutes and volume steps that run omarchy-audio-output-volume write 0. On quattro (finding 1 of the same comment) the plain Mute/Volume keys on an alsa_output.* default sink and audio-panel mutes do not run the script and write nothing. The write also happens only where a platform::mute node exists. The draft contradicts its own first finding here.

flags.claim: From source, the trigger follows PipeWire's default hardware mute
flags.why: My evidence supports 'should follow', and only on HDA ThinkPads whose codec driver applies the ThinkPad fixup, for a hardware-mixer ALSA sink. Both user reports (the PR author and issue #11005) say the LED stays dark, and my report states the source expectation conflicts with them. As written, the sentence reads as established fact and omits the contradiction, even with 'Not tested on hardware' following.

flags.claim: Why the two user reports differ was not settled.
flags.why: Wrong subject. The two reports agree: the LED stays dark. They differ only in the trigger reading, and the previous sentence already gives a candidate explanation for [none] (an earlier write of 0). What was not settled is why both see a dark LED when the source says the trigger should follow PipeWire's hardware mute. My report: 'Why the reports differ [from the source expectation] is not settled here.'

flags.claim: Drive the LED from the media service on default-sink mute changes, which also covers the audio panel.
flags.why: The audio panel mutes its volumeSink, the physical sink resolved through omarchy-audio-output-sink. That equals the default sink only when the default is an ALSA sink. With a DSP or EasyEffects default, the panel mutes the physical sink behind it, and the media service's volumeSink is null for non-ALSA defaults, so a default-sink handler would miss it. The suggestion is also untested (no QML was run).

flags.claim: Write only when brightness differs from the wanted state.
flags.why: A qualifier was lost. My report adds that the timing between PipeWire's ALSA switch write and the read-back is untested, so the trigger may not have updated brightness yet when the script reads it. The suggestion is sound as a direction, but it is untested.

flags.claim: (Verified, sandbox) ... an unresolved sink makes no LED write.
flags.why: The debounce and unknown-action cases were run (probes P2, P8), but the unresolved-sink case was not. It is established by source reading only (the script exits 1 at L18-21, before the LED block at L84-88), yet it is listed under 'Verified (sandbox ...)'.

flags.claim: The LED then follows only ALT+Volume or non-ALSA sinks.
flags.why: 'Only' describes this PR's LED sync. Where the kernel audio-mute trigger works (finding 2), the LED still follows the in-shell mute through the trigger until a script write of 0 detaches it. 'Non-ALSA sinks' means a default sink whose name does not start with alsa_output.

flags.claim: Each raise or lower press ... now adds one pactl get-sink-mute, one helper process and one brightnessctl write of 0 ... Computing the mute state once and skipping unchanged writes would avoid this.
flags.why: Three things are too strong. (1) On quattro this applies only to presses that run the script (ALT+Volume, non-ALSA default); at the PR's merge-base it applies to all raise/lower presses. (2) The brightnessctl write happens only where a platform::mute node exists. (3) Only 'raise' was measured (probe P1); 'lower' goes through the same code. 'Would avoid this' is partial: the helper process still spawns unless the check is done inline.

flags.claim: ... when the default sink is not an alsa_output.* sink (Bluetooth, a DSP chain, EasyEffects).
flags.why: The fallback rule (any default not named alsa_output.*) is checked (Service.qml L469, shell.qml L1591-1592), and the #13424 commit message names DSP chains and EasyEffects. 'Bluetooth' is inferred from PipeWire's bluez_output.* node naming and was not run. Low risk.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** On current `quattro` the Mute and Volume keys bypass this PR's script, so the LED misses them on laptop speakers.

### Keys bypass the script on `quattro`

Since #13424, `handleVolumeKey()` in `shell/plugins/services/media/Service.qml` handles these keys itself when the default sink is `alsa_output.*`. This PR's LED update then runs only for ALT+Volume or non-ALSA sinks.

**Suggested change:** Drive the LED from the media service on default-sink mute changes.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails on quattro b421b1b4 plus this PR, where the PR's test still passes because it calls the script directly)</summary>


Tree: `quattro` at b421b1b4 with this PR's three files applied (the PR merges cleanly; none of its files changed on `quattro` since the merge-base). Save as `test/shell.d/mute-key-led-path-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/mute-key-led-path-test.sh` (needs `lua`, as `test/shell.d/shell-shortcuts-test.sh` on `quattro` does).

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# The hardware volume keys must reach code that drives the platform::mute LED.
# Loads the default bindings against a stub hl, the way
# test/shell.d/shell-shortcuts-test.sh does.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

require_command lua

bindings=$(HOME="$(mktemp -d)" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" lua <<'LUA'
package.path = os.getenv("OMARCHY_PATH") .. "/?.lua;" .. package.path
local function proxy()
  return setmetatable({}, {
    __index = function(self, key) local v = proxy(); rawset(self, key, v); return v end,
    __call = function() return {} end,
  })
end
local dsp = proxy()
rawset(dsp, "global", function(name) return { global = name } end)
rawset(dsp, "exec_cmd", function(command) return { exec = command } end)
hl = setmetatable({
  dsp = dsp,
  bind = function(keys, dispatcher)
    local kind, target = "other", ""
    if type(dispatcher) == "table" and dispatcher.global then kind, target = "global", dispatcher.global
    elseif type(dispatcher) == "table" and dispatcher.exec then kind, target = "exec", dispatcher.exec end
    print(keys .. "\t" .. kind .. "\t" .. target)
  end,
}, { __index = function() return function() return {} end end })
require("default.hypr.helpers")
dofile(os.getenv("OMARCHY_PATH") .. "/default/hypr/bindings/media.lua")
LUA
)

shell_drives_led=false
if grep -rqE 'platform::mute|omarchy-brightness-keyboard-mute' "$ROOT/shell" 2>/dev/null; then
  shell_drives_led=true
fi

for key in XF86AudioMute XF86AudioRaiseVolume XF86AudioLowerVolume; do
  line=$(grep -E "^$key"$'\t' <<<"$bindings")
  if [[ $line == *$'\texec\tomarchy-audio-output-volume '* ]]; then
    pass "$key runs omarchy-audio-output-volume, which syncs the mute LED"
  elif $shell_drives_led; then
    pass "$key is handled in the shell, which syncs the mute LED"
  else
    fail "$key reaches code that syncs the mute LED" "$line"
  fi
done
```

Actual output on `quattro` b421b1b4 + this PR (exit 1):

```
XF86AudioMute	global	omarchy:audio.mute-toggle
not ok - XF86AudioMute reaches code that syncs the mute LED
```

Actual output on the PR head d6e303b7 (its merge-base still binds the keys to the script; exit 0):

```
ok - XF86AudioMute runs omarchy-audio-output-volume, which syncs the mute LED
ok - XF86AudioRaiseVolume runs omarchy-audio-output-volume, which syncs the mute LED
ok - XF86AudioLowerVolume runs omarchy-audio-output-volume, which syncs the mute LED
```

Why: #13424 (merged to `quattro` after this PR was opened) binds these keys to shell global shortcuts (`default/hypr/bindings/media.lua` lines 2-4, `default/omarchy/shortcuts` lines 29-31). `shell/shell.qml` lines 1589-1592 call `media.handleVolumeKey()` first and only run `omarchy-audio-output-volume` when it returns false. `handleVolumeKey()` in `shell/plugins/services/media/Service.qml` (lines 474-504) sets `audio.muted` over PipeWire and returns true whenever the default sink's name starts with `alsa_output.` (line 469), which is the usual laptop-speaker case. `quattro`'s own tests assert this (`test/shell.d/shell-shortcuts-test.sh` line 98, "the mute key toggles mute in the shell"; `test/shell.d/media-test.sh` line 66). The PR's own test still passes on this tree because it calls the script directly:

```
ok - muting the output lights the mute indicator
ok - unmuting the output clears the mute indicator
ok - raising volume unmutes and clears the mute indicator
ok - a missing LED node leaves the mute key working
ok - the mic path still drives the mic-mute LED
ok - unmuting the mic clears the mic-mute LED
ok - the helper drives an explicitly named LED
ok - an unknown state is rejected
```

On `quattro` + this PR the script (and so the LED sync) still runs for `ALT + XF86AudioRaiseVolume/LowerVolume` (`+1`/`-1`) and when the default sink is not an `alsa_output.*` sink (Bluetooth, a DSP chain, EasyEffects).
</details>

### Writing 0 detaches the `audio-mute` trigger

On ThinkPads `platform::mute` defaults to the `audio-mute` trigger, which the kernel removes on any write of 0, as each unmute or step through the script now does. From source, the trigger should follow PipeWire's hardware mute on HDA ThinkPads, so other mutes would stop reaching the LED. Not tested on hardware.

**Suggested change:** Write only when `brightness` differs from the wanted state.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Source for the trigger finding** (not reproduced; needs a ThinkPad whose `platform::mute/trigger` shows `[audio-mute]`):

- Linux `drivers/leds/led-class.c` `brightness_store()`: `if (state == LED_OFF) led_trigger_remove(led_cdev);`
- Linux `drivers/platform/x86/lenovo/thinkpad_acpi.c`: `platform::mute` has `.default_trigger = "audio-mute"`.
- Linux `sound/core/control_led.c` fires the speaker LED trigger from controls marked `SPK_LED`. On HDA ThinkPads, `sound/hda/codecs/generic.c` marks "Master Playback Switch" that way.
- PipeWire's ACP mutes a hardware-mixer sink through the path's Master switch (`analog-output-speaker.conf`, UCM `PlaybackMasterElem`) unless `api.alsa.soft-mixer` is set, which Omarchy sets only on ASUS ROG.
- A `trigger` reading of `[none]` is also the state any earlier write of 0 leaves behind. Issue #11005 reports `[audio-mute]` on an X1 Carbon Gen 9. Both the PR author and #11005 report that the LED stays dark on mute, which the source does not explain; that was not settled.
- The suggested read-before-write is untested: the trigger's update may lag PipeWire's switch write.

**Verified** (sandbox, stubbed audio and LED tools, at `d6e303b`):

- Mute-toggle writes `set 1` when muted and `set 0` when unmuted. Raise, lower and ±N unmute and write `set 0`.
- A debounced second toggle or an unknown action makes no LED write (an unresolved sink exits before the LED code, from source).
- With `brightnessctl` failing or absent, or no LED node, the key still mutes, shows the OSD and exits 0.
- `omarchy-audio-input-mute` still drives `platform::micmute`. An empty device argument falls back to it.
- The new test runs under `test/shell`, passes at the head and fails at the merge-base on its first case.

**Optional notes:**

- Each raise or lower press that runs the script now adds one `pactl get-sink-mute`, one helper process and, where the LED node exists, one `brightnessctl` write of 0, before the OSD (stub log for `raise`: 6 `pactl` and 1 `brightnessctl` call, against 5 and 0 at the merge-base). Computing the mute state once and skipping unchanged writes would reduce this.
- Open #6897 also writes `platform::mute`, from a PipeWire watcher that writes only on change. If both merge, two writers own the same LED.
</details>
